es: Resumir en una frase las preguntas de una entrevista con enquire about, want to know, be asked to y probe.

teaching.en: Interviewers often enquire about your volunteer work, and you may then be asked to describe one project in enough detail for them to see your part in it.
teaching.es: Los entrevistadores suelen preguntar por tu trabajo de voluntariado, y luego puede que te pidan describir un proyecto con el detalle suficiente para ver cuál fue tu papel.
teaching.explanationEs: Enquire about + nombre resume una pregunta sobre un tema. Be asked to + verbo recoge una petición.
segments: Interviewers often enquire about your volunteer work, and you may then be asked to
describe one project in enough detail for them to see your part in it.
teaching.audioText: Interviewers often enquire about your volunteer work, and you may then be asked to describe one project in enough detail for them to see your part in it.

teaching.en: Interviewers usually want to know whether you can work at weekends, so a short account says that they wanted to know whether I could.
teaching.es: Los entrevistadores suelen querer saber si puedes trabajar los fines de semana, así que un relato breve dice que querían saber si yo podía.
teaching.explanationEs: Want to know + whether + sujeto + verbo: pregunta de sí o no, sin did ni inversión; el tiempo retrocede.
segments: Interviewers usually want to know whether you can work at weekends, so
a short account says that they wanted to know whether I could.
teaching.audioText: Interviewers usually want to know whether you can work at weekends, so a short account says that they wanted to know whether I could.

teaching.en: If a panel decides to probe your reasons, it may query a detail that looked vague in your first answer.
teaching.es: Si un comité decide indagar en tus razones, puede cuestionar un dato que parecía vago en tu primera respuesta.
teaching.explanationEs: Probe es seguir preguntando sobre lo mismo; query pone en duda un dato concreto.
segments: If a panel decides to probe your reasons, it may
query a detail that looked vague in your first answer.
teaching.audioText: If a panel decides to probe your reasons, it may query a detail that looked vague in your first answer.

teaching.en: A concise report keeps the meaning and skips the small talk: They asked why I had applied and how long I had worked there.
teaching.es: Un informe conciso conserva el sentido y omite la charla superficial: Preguntaron por qué había solicitado y cuánto tiempo llevaba trabajando allí.
teaching.explanationEs: Con wh- el orden es afirmativo (why I had applied) y el tiempo retrocede un paso.
segments: A concise report keeps the meaning and skips the small talk: They
asked why I had applied and how long I had worked there.
teaching.audioText: A concise report keeps the meaning and skips the small talk: They asked why I had applied and how long I had worked there.

teaching.en: Some interviewers zero in on a single point and press for details, so after the interview I wrote a short report of each exchange.
teaching.es: Algunos entrevistadores se centran en un solo punto e insisten en pedir detalles, así que después de la entrevista escribí un informe breve de cada intercambio.
teaching.explanationEs: Zero in on + nombre: concentrarse en un punto; press for + nombre: insistir en pedirlo.
segments: Some interviewers zero in on a single point and press for details,
so after the interview I wrote a short report of each exchange.
teaching.audioText: Some interviewers zero in on a single point and press for details, so after the interview I wrote a short report of each exchange.

teaching.en: When a panel decides to delve into your motives, your report should name the topic first and then say what they wanted to know about it.
teaching.es: Cuando un comité decide profundizar en tus motivos, tu informe debe nombrar primero el tema y luego decir qué querían saber sobre él.
teaching.explanationEs: Delve into + nombre: profundizar en un asunto. El informe ordena tema y pregunta.
segments: When a panel decides to delve into your motives, your report should name
the topic first and then say what they wanted to know about it.
teaching.audioText: When a panel decides to delve into your motives, your report should name the topic first and then say what they wanted to know about it.

prompt.es: Completa: «Querían saber si podía trabajar los fines de semana.»

feedback.es: Las preguntas de sí o no se cuentan con whether o if + sujeto + verbo, sin did ni inversión; el verbo retrocede a could.

hint.es: Es la palabra que introduce una pregunta de sí o no dentro de una frase; if también sirve.

origin.text: After the interview, Tom's mother asks what the panel was interested in. Tom answers, «They wanted to know ___ I could work at weekends.»

prompt.es: ¿Cómo se resume la pregunta del comité en una sola frase?

choices.text: They enquired about my experience of working with children.
They enquired about what was my experience of working with children.
They wanted to know that my experience of working with children was.

feedback.es: Enquire about + nombre resume la pregunta sobre un tema en un solo verbo. Las otras conservan la inversión o usan that en lugar de una pregunta indirecta.

hint.es: Busca el verbo que va seguido directamente del tema, sin repetir la pregunta entera.

origin.text: The scholarship panel turned to Mia and asked: «What is your experience of working with children?» Later, she had to report the question to her teacher.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Me pidieron que describiera un proyecto con detalle.»

answer.text: I was asked to describe one project in detail

feedback.es: Be asked to + verbo base recoge una petición en voz pasiva: I was asked to describe… resume la orden del comité.

hint.es: Empieza por I was asked y continúa con el verbo base.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué querían saber en segundo lugar sobre Leo.

choices.text: Why he preferred teaching at night.
Whether he was available to work at night.
How long he had taught in total.

feedback.es: Primero preguntaron por su experiencia docente y en segundo lugar quisieron saber si podía trabajar de noche. No preguntaron por preferencias ni por años.

origin.audio: After the interview, Leo told us what the panel had wanted to know. First, they enquired about his experience of teaching, and then they wanted to know whether he could work at night. After that, he was asked to describe the most difficult class he had ever taught. When he answered, one panel member probed his decision to change the lesson plan halfway through, asking why he had waited so long. Leo said that, looking back, he should have asked for help earlier. Overall, he felt that the questions had been fair, although the last one had made him nervous.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez. ¿Qué hizo el miembro del comité que «probed» su decisión?

choices.text: He asked Leo to repeat his first answer.
He offered to help Leo to write a better lesson plan.
He asked Leo to justify a decision he had made.

feedback.es: Indagar en la decisión de cambiar el plan es seguir preguntando por qué esperó tanto: le pide que la justifique, no que repita ni le ofrece ayuda.

origin.audio: After the interview, Leo told us what the panel had wanted to know. First, they enquired about his experience of teaching, and then they wanted to know whether he could work at night. After that, he was asked to describe the most difficult class he had ever taught. When he answered, one panel member probed his decision to change the lesson plan halfway through, asking why he had waited so long. Leo said that, looking back, he should have asked for help earlier. Overall, he felt that the questions had been fair, although the last one had made him nervous.

prompt.es: Completa: «Querían preguntar por mi experiencia de trabajo en el extranjero.»

feedback.es: Enquire about + nombre es el verbo de informe para preguntar por un tema; tras wished to va la forma base.

origin.text: In my notes for the tutor I wrote that the panel wished to ___ about my experience of working abroad, and that they did not ask anything about my studies.

prompt.es: Resume en una frase cada una de las tres preguntas del comité.

answer.text: They wanted to know why I had chosen that course. They asked whether I could start in May. I was asked to describe my last job.
accepted: They wanted to know why I had chosen that course. They asked whether I could start in May. I was asked to describe my last job.
The panel enquired why I had chosen the course and whether I could start in May, and I was asked to describe my last job.

feedback.es: Las tres frases cuentan la pregunta con estilo indirecto: why + orden afirmativo, whether + could y be asked to + verbo.

origin.text: El comité te hizo tres preguntas: 1) «Why did you choose this course?» 2) «Can you start in May?» 3) «Describe your last job.» Cuéntalas después en pasado, una frase cada una, con estilo indirecto.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender este relato sobre el interés del comité?

choices.text: That it wanted proof that the candidate had led others, not just experience.
That it cared about results more than about the candidate's own role.
That it wanted to know how long the candidate had volunteered.

feedback.es: Insistir en si había liderado un equipo indica que busca pruebas concretas de liderazgo, no experiencia general; el comité no cuestiona el voluntariado ni pregunta por su duración, y el papel de la candidata es justo lo que explora.

origin.text: The panel enquired about my volunteer work for ten minutes and wanted to know whether I had ever led a team. When I described my project, one member probed my reasons, and I was asked to explain why I had not asked for help.

prompt.es: Escucha la pregunta del comité y elige el informe más fiel.

choices.text: They wanted to know that I could start in September and what prevented me.
They wanted to know whether I would be able to start in September and what would stop me.
They asked me could I start in September and what would prevent me from coming.

feedback.es: El informe fiel usa whether + would be able y what would stop me con orden afirmativo; las otras mantienen la inversión o cambian la pregunta en una afirmación.

origin.audio: Could you tell us whether you would be able to start in September and, if not, what would prevent you from doing so?

prompt.es: Ordena: «El comité preguntó por mis planes después del curso.»

answer.text: The panel enquired about my plans after the course

feedback.es: Enquire about + nombre resume la pregunta: the panel enquired about my plans, y after the course precisa el momento.

prompt.es: Mia debe contar las dos preguntas a su profesor. ¿Qué informe es fiel?

choices.text: They wanted to know how long did I work with children and why did I leave my previous post.
They enquired about how long have I worked with children and why I left my previous post.
They wanted to know how long I had worked with children and why I had left my previous post.

feedback.es: Las dos preguntas se cuentan con orden afirmativo y un paso atrás: have worked pasa a had worked y did you leave a had left. Las otras mantienen la inversión.

origin.text: Original questions from the panel: «How long have you worked with children? Why did you leave your previous post?» Mia must now report both questions to her teacher in one sentence.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué sugiere sobre cómo se sintió Carlos.

choices.text: That the constant questions put him under pressure.
That he thought the panel was poorly prepared.
That he felt relaxed because the questions were predictable.

feedback.es: Carlos dice que el comité «no dejaba de presionarle» con preguntas cada vez más concretas: se sintió bajo presión por su insistencia, no orgulloso ni crítico con su preparación.

origin.audio: After the interview, Carlos complained that the panel had kept pressing him. They enquired about his reasons for leaving his last job, then they wanted to know whether the company had asked him to go, and finally one of them probed his answer by asking why he had not mentioned it in his application.

prompt.es: Completa: «El entrevistador insistió en pedir más detalles del proyecto.»

feedback.es: Press for + nombre es la colocación para insistir en pedir algo; con on significaría presionar sobre una persona o un asunto.

origin.text: I gave a vague answer, so the interviewer decided to press ___ more details about the project before moving on to the next question.
